'''Hessy Levinsons Taft''' (born '''Hessy Lewinsohn'''; 17 May 1934 – 1 January 2026) was a [[German Jew]] who was featured as an infant in [[Propaganda in Nazi Germany|Nazi propaganda]] after her photo won a contest to find "the most beautiful [[Aryan race|Aryan]] baby" in 1935. Taft's image was subsequently distributed widely by the [[Nazi Party]] in a variety of materials, such as magazines and postcards, to promote [[Aryanism]].

==Photograph==
Hessy Lewinsohn was born in [[Berlin]], [[Nazi Germany]] on 17 May 1934.<ref>{{Cite web|date=15 February 1990|title=Oral history interview with Hessy Levinsons Taft|url=http://collections.ushmm.org/search/catalog/irn504720|url-status=live|publisher=[[United States Holocaust Memorial Museum]]|accessdate=31 August 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150831230427/http://collections.ushmm.org/search/catalog/irn504720|archivedate=31 August 2015}}</ref> Her [[Ashkenazi Jewish]] parents, Jacob Lewinsohn and Pauline Lewinsohn (née Levine),<ref name=nyt/><ref>{{Cite news|url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/morning-mix/wp/2014/07/07/the-perfect-aryan-child-the-nazis-used-in-propaganda-was-actually-jewish/|title = The 'perfect Aryan' child used in Nazi propaganda was actually Jewish|date = 7 July 2014|accessdate = 31 August 2015|newspaper = [[The Washington Post]]|last = McCoy|first = Terrence}}</ref> were opera singers<ref name="nyt" /> originally from [[Latvia]]. (The family's surname was later changed to Levinsons.<ref name=nyt/>) Unaware that their daughter's photographer had entered the photograph into the contest, they accidentally learned that it had been selected by Nazi [[Reichs Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda|Propaganda Minister]] [[Joseph Goebbels]] as the winner.

Fearing that the [[Nazis]] would discover that their family was [[Jewish]], Pauline Lewinsohn demanded that the photographer explain the situation. The photographer, Hans Ballin, told her that he knew they were Jewish and deliberately entered Hessy Lewinsohn's photograph into the contest because he "wanted to make the Nazis ridiculous".<ref name=nyt/><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/germany/10938062/Nazi-perfect-Aryan-poster-child-was-Jewish.html|title = Nazi 'perfect Aryan' poster child was Jewish|date = 1 July 2014|accessdate = 31 August 2015|website = [[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|last = Huggler|first = Justin|location = Berlin|archivedate = 31 August 2015|url-status = live|archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20150831232521/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/germany/10938062/Nazi-perfect-Aryan-poster-child-was-Jewish.html}}</ref> In July 2014, Taft told the German-language newspaper ''[[Bild]]'' that "I can laugh about it now, but if the Nazis had known who I really was, I wouldn't be alive."<ref name=bild>{{Cite web|url = http://www.bild.de/regional/berlin/adolf-hitler/berliner-juedin-hessy-taft-war-hitlers-propaganda-baby-36611794.bild.html|title = Ich war Hitlers Propaganda-Baby|date = 1 July 2014|accessdate = 31 August 2015|website = [[Bild]]|last = Sidon|first = Adi|trans-title = I Was Hitler's Propaganda Baby|language = German}}</ref>

==Later life and death==
In 1937, the family returned to Latvia, keeping the story of the photo a secret to protect themselves from retribution.<ref name=nyt/> In 1938, Jacob Levinsons was briefly arrested by the [[SS]]. In the same year, the family migrated to France and settled in [[Paris]]. After the Nazis occupied Paris in 1940, they fled to [[Nice]] and then to [[Republic of Cuba (1902–1959)|Cuba]]. In 1949, they moved to New York City.<ref name=bild/><ref name=nyt/>

Hessy Levinsons studied chemistry at [[Julia Richman High School]] in New York, and majored in chemistry at [[Barnard College]],<ref name=acs/> graduating in 1955.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://barnard.edu/sites/default/files/alumnae_biographical_files_inventory.pdf|title=Alumnae Biographical Files|publisher=Barnard College Archives|accessdate=16 July 2019|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304072834/http://barnard.edu/sites/default/files/alumnae_biographical_files_inventory.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Class of 1955|url=https://our.barnard.edu/s/1133/16/index.aspx?sid=1133&gid=1&pgid=3087|access-date=2 September 2021|website=our.barnard.edu|language=en}}</ref> As a graduate student in chemistry at [[Columbia University]], she met her husband, mathematics instructor [[Earl Taft]]. She and her husband joined the faculty at [[Rutgers University]], but she left academia to raise a family, later working on the [[AP Chemistry]] exam for the [[Educational Testing Service]] (ETS).<ref name=acs/>

After 30 years at ETS, she returned to New York as a chemistry professor at [[St. John's University (New York City)|St. John's University]]<ref name=":0" /><ref name=acs>{{cite magazine|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/92/i36/Hessy-Taft.html|journal=Chemical & Engineering News|publisher=American Chemical Society|title=Hessy Taft: Jewish survivor and longtime ACS member describes how she was once a Nazi poster child|volume=92|issue=36|date=8 September 2014|page=30|first=Lauren K.|last=Wolf}}</ref> in 2000. Her research in this later period of life focused on [[Sustainability#Water|water sustainability]]. She retired in 2016.<ref>Author biography from {{cite journal|last1=Alexandratos|first1=Spiro D.|last2=Barak|first2=Naty|last3=Bauer|first3=Diana|last4=Davidson|first4=F. Todd|last5=Gibney|first5=Brian R.|last6=Hubbard|first6=Susan S.|last7=Taft|first7=Hessy L.|last8=Westerhof|first8=Paul|date=January 2019|doi=10.1021/acssuschemeng.8b05859|issue=3|journal=ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering|pages=2879–2888|publisher=American Chemical Society|title=Sustaining Water Resources: Environmental and Economic Impact|volume=7|osti=<!-- DO NOT ADD LINKS TO PREPRINT VERSIONS THAT DO NOT INCLUDE THE AUTHOR BIOGRAPHY -->|s2cid=104330272|url=<!-- DO NOT ADD LINKS TO PREPRINT VERSIONS THAT DO NOT INCLUDE THE AUTHOR BIOGRAPHY -->}}</ref>

Taft died at her home in [[San Francisco]], on 1 January 2026, at the age of 91.<ref name=nyt>{{cite news |last1=Rosenwald |first1=Michael S. |title=Hessy Levinsons Taft, Jewish Baby on Cover of Nazi Magazine, Dies at 91 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/09/world/europe/hessy-levinsons-taft-dead.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=9 January 2026 |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref>
